key_insight: Portable query generation works best when reward shaping is made robust, because the main gains come from preventing reward-hacking rather than from the choice of optimizer.
engineering_relevance: For industrial semantic job search, the practical takeaway is to harden reward rules and judges so generated queries preserve qualifications without leaking seeker-specific identifiers.
method: Built an end-to-end RLAIF pipeline for portable job-search query generation.
Compared critic-free optimizers (RLOO, REINFORCE++) with GRPO under adversarial reward conditions.
Added a deterministic rule-based reward floor to penalize verbatim-copying and stabilize training.
evidence_signal: On cross-family evaluation, the rule-based reward floor improved quality by +0.147, and the training-time reward model inflated apparent gains by 2.4×.
watch_item: The approach is sensitive to reward-specification quality, so poorly designed LLM-as-judge rubrics can still induce degenerate copying behavior.
paper_title: Designing Reward Signals for Portable Query Generation: A Case Study in Industrial Semantic Job Search
